research_question: Do the MMECG findings -- template-saturated beat metrics and a timing-dominated continuous gap -- hold on CW radar, and is the timing error a per-subject systematic latency (EMAT-like, calibratable) or per-beat jitter?
no_training: Frozen seed-42 test predictions and training-fold labels only; nothing is trained, tuned or selected.

inputs.row_alignment: prediction rows equal test.h5 rows; verified by exact equality of stored ground truth

analyses.A1_scenario_readout: CR_RVS continuous metrics per scenario (Resting / Valsalva / Apnea; stored codes NB / IB / SP) with the frozen evaluator functions; Resting-only is the like-for-like comparison with the cited literature
analyses.A2_tier1_template_floor: Tier-1 Shape-200 readout of the three CR_RVS models and the training-label template floor on the same test beats, centre cycle cut by GT R peaks (identical definition to the MMECG readout)
analyses.A3_template_timing: training-fold template placed at GT peaks (T0, oracle), REM-Net event-head peaks (T1), REM-Net waveform peaks (T2), Chen-TCN waveform peaks (T3), WaveGRU-Net waveform peaks (T4); T4 is added for MMECG too, leaving T0-T3 unchanged
analyses.A4_timing_error_decomposition: radar-derived peaks matched to GT R peaks within +/-150 ms; signed offset radar minus GT decomposed into global bias, per-subject bias spread and within-subject jitter; match rate
analyses.A5_bias_corrected_oracle: T1 and T3 peaks shifted by each test subject's own median offset (GT-derived, ORACLE) before placing the template; the recovery toward T0 measures how much of the gap a perfect per-subject latency calibration could remove

pre_declared_readings: If A5 recovers most of the gap between T1/T3 and T0, the bottleneck is a per-subject systematic latency (EMAT-like) that calibration could address.
If A5 recovers little, the bottleneck is within-subject jitter that no constant offset can remove.
EMAT is not identified by any of these analyses; a per-subject offset is only compatible with an electromechanical delay among other causes.
statistics: fold-macro with population std; CR_RVS has 5 folds, so paired comparisons report fold wins and effect sizes, not Wilcoxon p-values
